title: Faraday pattern formation in dipolar superfluid and supersolid quantum gases
authors: Sumit Semwal, Shawan K. Jha, G. A. Bougas, S. I. Mistakidis, Pankaj Kumar Mishra
abstract: We investigate Faraday instabilities in three-dimensional parametrically driven trapped dipolar quantum gases within the framework of the extended Gross-Pitaevskii equation. In the superfluid regime, periodic modulation of the short-range interactions induces the resonant excitation of discrete polygonal surface modes displaying sub-harmonic response. The resonance frequencies and the parametric windows of instability are accurately captured by an appropriate Mathieu equation, further corroborating our simulations. It is also shown that dipolar interactions in superfluids shift the resonance frequencies to lower values compared to their non-dipolar counterparts. Near the superfluid-to-supersolid transition, intrinsic density undulations associated with the softened roton mode accelerate pattern formation, yielding hybrid surface and bulk excitations. The bulk patterns prevail deeper in the supersolid regime, emerging from droplet collisions with the superfluid background. Our results reveal a crossover from surface collective modes to hybrid surface-bulk excitations and demonstrate how parametric driving dictates pattern formation in long-range interacting quantum fluids.
summary: This paper investigates how external parametric driving induces Faraday patterns in dipolar quantum gases across different phases. It uses the extended Gross-Pitaevskii equation to model the system, revealing a distinct crossover mechanism: surface modes dominate in the superfluid phase, transitioning through hybrid excitations near the supersolid boundary, and finally settling into bulk droplet patterns characteristic of the supersolid state.
main_problem: The study investigates Faraday instabilities, which manifest as spontaneous structure formation, in dipolar superfluid and supersolid quantum gases subjected to external parametric driving.
main_result: The research demonstrates a clear dynamical crossover from surface collective modes (superfluids) to hybrid surface-bulk excitations near the transition, culminating in bulk density patterns characteristic of the supersolid regime.
method: The dynamics are simulated using the extended Gross-Pitaevskii equation (eGPE), and resonance spectra are analyzed by deriving an appropriate Mathieu equation.
model_or_system: The system models three-dimensional trapped dipolar quantum gases, such as $^{164}	ext{Dy}$ atoms. The physics is governed by the competition between short-range interactions, long-range anisotropic dipole-dipole interactions (DDI), and external parametric driving.
key_observables: Faraday patterns (standing-wave density modulations), resonance frequencies, sub-harmonic response, and the characterization of surface vs. bulk excitations.
important_parameters: The relative strength of contact vs. dipolar interactions ($\epsilon_{dd}$), the trap aspect ratio, and the parameters governing the parametric driving protocol ($A$, $\omega_d$).
main_assumptions: The dynamics are modeled using the extended Gross-Pitaevskii equation (eGPE), which includes beyond mean-field Lee-Huang-Yang corrections in the local-density approximation.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates distinct ground state phases (supersolid vs. superfluid) based on scattering length, while Figure 2 shows various surface density patterns ($\ell=2$ to $\ell=6$) induced by parametric resonance via scattering length modulation.
paper_structure: The paper analyzes the system in different regimes: first addressing the superfluid phase where discrete polygonal surface modes are excited; then examining the transition region near the supersolid state, leading to hybrid excitations; and finally characterizing the bulk patterns that dominate deep within the supersolid regime.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it explores pattern formation and dynamical instabilities in strongly interacting quantum fluids using advanced mean-field theory, bridging concepts from superfluidity, dipolar interactions, and non-equilibrium dynamics.
